why: Several items call for attacking a rival's logo, and the scheme splits destroying a rival's work (T3-006) from turning it into the room's own sign (T3-068) with no explicit marker beyond the replacement proposed.

why.T3-028: The codes edit, update and continually tweak a browser script that maintains the G unattended, i.e. running a script for the room's own work, not arguing whether scripts are fair (T3-027).

why.T3-031: The single code plays the room's own running observation/joke that its canvas area is shaping to look like Wisconsin, an in-joke about the room's work rather than an attack, a report or a mark being placed.

why.T3-005: The codes report rival colours appearing and the work wrecked and call people over to fight back and preserve the G, an attack under way and the room's answer, not mere watching and fixing (T3-021) nor tracing the attacker (T3-087).

why.T3-076: The codes tell the room's own members to build their G instead of attacking the Bears, warn that recruiting defacement gets bans, and call off attacks, i.e. reining in the room's attackers, not refusing to cover unasked (T3-024).

why.T3-037: The codes judge the canvas as a whole as data gathering disguised as fun and as nonsense, dismissing its worth, rather than arguing the fairness of scripts as such (T3-027) or objecting to canvas posts crowding the sub (T3-075).

why.T3-006: Most codes call for or celebrate destroying/erasing the Bears work (delete and replace with the G, BEARS SUCK, helping Finland draw over them, abolishing them).
why.T3-068: Three codes specifically turn another room's art into the room's own sign: turn the Bears logo into the Pack logo, Packerize the Bear symbol, recruit to make it a Packers logo.

multiplacement_log.why_not_one: T3-006 alone would drop the codes that alter the Bears logo into the room's own sign (Packerized, turned into the Pack logo), which its destroy/erase gate does not reach.
multiplacement_log.why_this_one: C0608261, C0777874 and C0738527 directly turn another room's art into the room's own sign, satisfying T3-068's gate, distinct from the destroying concepts that stay with T3-006.
multiplacement_log.dispensable: T3-068: if forced to one, the conversion-of-rival-art reading would be lost and only the destruction of the Bears work would remain.

why.T3-149: The codes stop attacks and carry a truce request to the Vikings sub, announce an agreement and a shared compromise, i.e. a pact ending or forestalling a fight between rooms already in contact, rather than only settling a border where no fight began (T3-010).

why.T3-038: The codes place the G pixel by pixel and report the lines, blocks and border being started and finished, i.e. building the mark and reporting its progress, not the design being argued (T3-004) or the coordinates being circulated (T3-070).

why.T3-010: The codes move a neighbouring heart to make space, contact the green lattice about space, invite Jaguars into a disputed 4 and hold off neighbours, i.e. settling lines and space with neighbours where no fight is being made, not a truce ending a fight (T3-149).

why.T3-006: The codes call to destroy the Vikings, declare war and rewrite the SKOL into GO PACK GO, four Ls, SHIT or A HOLE, i.e. attacks meant to erase or black out another room's work, not simply growing into their space (T3-061) or a faction colour spread (T3-171).

why.T3-084: The single code carries a request for help with the G's coordinates to ELoE, another canvas group asked as a group for hands, rather than a call posted to a sub's membership (T3-062) or help sent to another's work (T3-011).

why.T3-015: The single code has the moderators contain all r/place talk in one hub thread, i.e. gathering canvas talk into one thread, not removing posts under a rule (T3-063) or members objecting to the flood (T3-075).

why.T3-028: As position 1: the codes edit, update and continually tweak a browser script that maintains the G unattended, running a script for the room's own work rather than arguing its fairness (T3-027).

why.T3-001: The codes circulate and praise a fabricated April Fools story and grade how hard it tried to look real, the room's own April Fools fake shared and revealed, rather than an official joke (T3-048) or an outside claim being tested (T3-095).
